description:
Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is a government initiative launched on January 25, 2008. 

The scheme aims to provide quality generic medicines at affordable prices to the masses. 

It is implemented by the Department of Pharmaceuticals under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. 

The initiative was launched to reduce the out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare for the common people. 

The primary objective is to ensure that essential medicines are available at a price that is affordable for all. 

The scheme aims to open a chain of Janaushadhi Kendras across the country. 

These Kendras are intended to provide generic medicines that are equivalent in quality to branded medicines. 

The government targets to establish over 10,500 Janaushadhi Kendras by March 2025. 

As of October 2023, there are over 8,000 Janaushadhi Kendras operational across India. 

The medicines available at these Kendras are sold at prices that are significantly lower than those of branded counterparts. 

For example, the cost of a generic medicine can be up to 90% less than that of a branded medicine. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of generic medicines among the public. 

This is to ensure that people are aware of the benefits of using generic medicines. 

The benefits of the scheme include improved access to essential medicines. 

It also includes the reduction of healthcare costs for patients. 

The scheme provides a wide range of medicines for various ailments. 

These include medicines for chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular diseases. 

The scheme also covers medicines for common ailments like fever, cold, and infections. 

The Janaushadhi Kendras also supply surgical items and consumables. 

The government has set a target to provide over 1,000 types of medicines through these Kendras. 

The medicines are sourced from various public sector undertakings and private manufacturers. 

The pricing of these medicines is regulated to ensure affordability. 

The scheme also provides incentives for entrepreneurs to open Janaushadhi Kendras. 

The government offers a one-time grant of ₹2 lakh to set up a Janaushadhi Kendra. 

Additionally, there is a provision for a margin of 20% on the sale of medicines. 

Eligibility to open a Janaushadhi Kendra includes being a registered pharmacist. 

The applicant must also have a minimum educational qualification of a diploma in pharmacy. 

The application process involves submitting an online application through the Janaushadhi website. 

Required documents include a copy of the pharmacy registration certificate. 

Applicants must also provide proof of educational qualifications. 

Once the application is submitted it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

If approved the applicant is notified and can proceed with setting up the Kendra. 

The timeline for approval can vary but is generally completed within 30 days. 

Disbursement of the one-time grant occurs after the Kendra is established. 

The government also conducts regular audits and inspections of the Kendras. 

This is to ensure compliance with the standards set for the sale of medicines. 

The scheme has seen significant growth since its inception. 

In the financial year 2022-2023 the sales from Janaushadhi Kendras reached approximately ₹1,200 crores. 

This indicates a growing acceptance of generic medicines among the public. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to promote the scheme. 

These campaigns aim to educate the public about the benefits of using generic medicines. 

The scheme has also contributed to the Make in India initiative. 

It encourages local manufacturing of medicines which boosts the economy. 

The Janaushadhi Kendras are strategically located in rural and semi-urban areas. 

This ensures that even the economically weaker sections have access to affordable medicines. 

The scheme has been instrumental in reducing the financial burden on families. 

It has also improved health outcomes by providing timely access to necessary medications. 

The government continues to expand the range of medicines available under the scheme. 

As of October 2023, there are over 1,500 types of generic medicines available. 

The scheme has been recognized internationally for its innovative approach to healthcare. 

It serves as a model for other countries looking to improve access to medicines. 

The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is a significant step towards universal health coverage. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The scheme aims to ensure that no one is left behind in accessing essential healthcare services. 

The government is committed to increasing the number of Kendras in the coming years. 

This will further enhance the reach and impact of the scheme. 

The success of the scheme is also reflected in the increasing number of beneficiaries. 

Millions of people have benefited from the availability of affordable medicines. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme for improvements. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account for future enhancements. 

The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is a transformative initiative. 

It plays a crucial role in the healthcare landscape of India. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to public health. 

It demonstrates a proactive approach to addressing healthcare challenges. 

The initiative has the potential to change the way healthcare is accessed in India. 

The focus on generic medicines is a significant shift in the pharmaceutical sector. 

It encourages competition among manufacturers leading to better pricing. 

The scheme has also created employment opportunities in the healthcare sector. 

Overall the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is a landmark initiative. 

It aims to make healthcare more inclusive and accessible for all citizens of India.
